transport: JSON-RPC 2.0 over the Unix socket or WebSocket (?token=...). Standard ACP methods pass through to the session's agent; _acpmux/* methods are the multiplexer's own.

acpNotes.initialize: The result's _meta.acpmux carries auth (the proof this connection presented, server/conn_auth.rs: localSocket|listenerToken|localApp|peerToken; a connection with none gets error -32001 for its first request and is closed), personInstance (this daemon run's id, which decision proofs bind; cx-0q7o), operations: string[] (the handoff and permission-group methods this daemon serves; clients gate each UI on its methods) and handoff: {maxCapsuleBytes: 65536}. features includes permissionGroups when permission groups are available.
acpNotes.session/new: params._meta.acpmux.ephemeral: true (acpmux run --ephemeral, acpmux exec) purges the session, as _acpmux/kill {purge: true} does, when the connection that created it closes (the client exits, or is killed mid-turn); a daemon restart before then keeps it, with a peer the flag is dropped and only the client's own kill purges, and an adopt is never tied to the connection. params._meta.acpmux.adopt {harness?: string, agentSessionId: string, ifLive?: "refuse" | "fork" | "open", watch?: boolean} adopts a Claude Code or Codex session started outside acpmux: the id must be a bare id found in the harness's own store (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or ~/.claude projects, CODEX_HOME or ~/.codex sessions), else invalid params. cwd defaults to the session's recorded cwd (Claude refuses a different one). The first turn resumes it (claude --resume, or session/load). Adopting an id twice returns the existing acpmux session. A session open in another process (the holder the harness records and that still runs: Codex's thread writer lock, a Claude Code session registry entry whose pid runs with its recorded start time, or for OpenCode a process outside acpmux whose command line names the id; a holder that has exited never counts) is refused with error data {reason: "adopt.live", details: {signal: "writerLock" | "registry" | "process", pid?, command?, canFork}} unless ifLive is "open" (adopt anyway) or "fork" (Claude only: a new conversation from claude --resume <id> --fork-session). Recorded as mux adopted {agentSessionId, fork?: true}. With watch true (Claude Code and Codex only) no harness starts and adopt.live does not apply: the chat shows the transcript and follows what the other app appends to it, its summary has watching: family, prompts are refused with data.reason watch.read_only, and it runs the conversation only after _acpmux/watch_take_over. A harness name that is a folder profile (.cmux/harnesses/<id>.toml in cwd or a parent; BRING-YOUR-OWN-HARNESS H4) that may not start yet is refused with invalid params; data {reason: harness.needs_trust (answer the folder's Trust question) | harness.needs_enable (show the Enable harness sheet: _acpmux/harness_enable), harness: string (the id), folder: string (the canonical folder that holds .cmux/harnesses)}. A Web or peer connection and an invalid file get no data. params._meta.acpmux.disallowedTools: string[] of Claude Code built-in tool names (letters, digits, _; anything else is invalid params) the chat never gets: kept in its meta as off tools rows tool:<name>, so every start of its Claude Code (the first, a respawn, a resume, a restart) passes --disallowedTools <name>; such a chat never claims a pooled harness. acpmux new --worktree, --prompt-file or --report-to sends ["AskUserQuestion"].
acpNotes.session/prompt: params._meta.acpmux {promptId?: string, steer?: boolean, provenance?: {kind: "agent_message", from: string, fromName?: string, to: string, msgId: string, threadId: string, replyTo?: string}}. provenance names the agent that sent the prompt (cmux agent message): each field one line, ids and addresses 1 to 256 bytes, fromName 1 to 64 characters, unknown fields dropped; it is recorded as _meta.provenance on the user_message (and queued) record, never sent to the agent. _meta.acpmux.fromSessionId and fromHarness (display only, never authority; prompt_provenance.rs FROM_SESSION_ID): the daemon stamps the sending session id and its harness family on an agent message's _meta.provenance (fromSessionId, fromHarness) when it bound them: the session the connection proved (caller token), or over a peer link only (Origin peer, no via) what the peer daemon or the mesh relay said of its own proven caller (the mesh relay carries no harness yet); a client's own values are dropped, never refused, and a forwarding daemon drops them before setting its own. _meta.acpmux.author {id: tailnet:<login> | user_<id> | guest:<id>, name, login?, node?, approval?: "owner"} (chat multiplayer: each field one line, approval only "owner", id, login and node 1 to 256 bytes, name 1 to 64 characters, unknown fields dropped, else author.value_refused) names the person who sent it: accepted over the unix socket and from a forwarding peer (servedAs peer, never via web), refused from Web and the app pane with author.origin_refused; recorded as _meta.provenance {kind: person_message, from: id, fromName: name, login?, node?} on user_message, queued and steer records, kept by that person's own queue_edit update, and forwarded to a peer as author. With approval "owner" (a link guest; provenance keeps approval: "owner") the prompt is queued, never steered in, whatever steer, steerNow or interrupt it asks, and waits for the owner: queued records awaitingOwner: true and revision: 0, prompt_accepted says awaitingOwner, and it runs only after _acpmux/queue_approve, in its place in the queue; at most 16 per author wait at once, else data.reason queue.too_many_held. Only the unix socket may send provenance, and the app pane a reply (replyTo set, from acp:<id> of another chat of this daemon, to acp:<the prompt's chat>; acpmux sets its fromName to that chat's own name): any other gets data.reason provenance.origin_refused, a malformed one provenance.value_refused; a prompt forwarded to a peer goes without it. On Claude Code harnesses a text block's cache_control reaches the API unchanged; other extra block fields are dropped. _meta.acpmux.class (block|question|result|fyi, or blocker (a block) and action (a result), the inbox's names; else invalid params with data.reason class.value_refused; acpmux send --class, prompt_class.rs) says what another agent's message asks of the chat: kept only on another agent's message (fromAgent, a provenance, or a connection that proved its session), where none means result (a lane report and a task result card are results too); the person's own prompt has none. It is recorded as class on the queued record and shown in queue rows; a queue_edit update drops it. It is checked before a peer's prompt is forwarded and when _acpmux/send_queue takes a send; a send that only the mesh relay reaches refuses any class but result (mesh.no_class), and a held agent-pair message keeps it and its sender when released. The response stays at the end of the turn and gains _meta.acpmux {promptId, turnId, turnSeq} next to the agent's own _meta. The prompting connection gets _acpmux/prompt_accepted as soon as the prompt is recorded.
acpNotes.session/cancel: A notification, as ACP defines it. Sent as a request (with an id) it is answered with {} once the cancel reaches the agent, also when no turn runs.
acpNotes.session/update: Live agent updates arrive with sessionId set to the acpmux id and _meta.acpmux {seq, at, kind} merged into the agent's own _meta (the agent's keys are kept). Subagent updates add _meta.acpmux.subagents[] entries; see SubagentEvent and WorkflowAgent. session/load replays add replay: true.

A start refused before the target records the prompt returns the record to draft and keeps its promptId, which a later start reuses by default. SessionSummary.inputSince: number|null (when the session began waiting on the person)
SessionSummary.subagentsWorkingSince: number|null (since when work the session started runs on past its own turn: a background subagent of its harness, or an open sub-session that runs a turn, waits on the person or has such work itself; its indicator and lane are working meanwhile, a task not being done until its subagents are; each change is a subagents_working record {since}, heard as session_changed)

SessionSummary.tools: ToolRow[]? (the chat's tools; present on per-session reads, attachments and ACP lists; omitted from census rows unless withTools is true. SessionSummary.usageWarnings: [{rule: noAutocompactCap|contextTokens|subagentsPerHour, value: number|null, limit: number|null, text: string, finding: string (text before its actions), actions: [{label: string, command: string, pending: string|null}]}] (the usage rules the session breaks under the config's usageWarnings thresholds, decided from usageStats when the summary is read; text is one line a tooltip shows, ending in the action, e.g. 90 subagents started in the last hour, above 40. (what its harness spends and holds, from the harness's own records: Claude Code's transcript and its subagents' transcripts, Codex's rollout; absent for any other harness, until its records are found, and from a peer on an older acpmux. UsageStats.note: A value acpmux could not read is null, never 0: the counts are null until the reads cover the whole last day (a first read cut short after the day began, a backlog not read yet, a file that could not be read). acpmux ls --wide prints null as ?.

LaneReportProvenance.note: The first line is [NAME] VERDICT at SHA12 · finding counts · turn N, STATE when the reply contains Review (who): SHIP|BLOCK|FIX|HOLD at a full SHA, including after prose. Counts cover following P1/P2/P3 finding starts; None means no findings. Otherwise the first sentence is limited to 120 characters at a word boundary. The body keeps whole lines up to about 600 characters and every P1/P2 finding's first sentence even past that budget. Session and commits are structured details, collapsed by the UI, not visible text. The daemon sends this at each turn end of a session the parent started; answer only if it needs you. Identity and turn/state come from provenance, never from the title. Legacy lane report: turn N ended titles remain readable. An authenticated parent waiting explicitly for the lane's completed turn, or reading its completed result through last/history, receives the same report as already read: archived without a new notification or queued turn. Anonymous/other-session reads do not suppress it; active parent turns are never cancelled.

daemon.readiness: acpmux daemon run serves the socket before reading session metadata and logs. _acpmux/status loading reports phase (loading-store, adopting, loading-logs, starting-agents, ready), sessionsLoaded and sessionsTotal (known so far during metadata discovery), and startupDone (the daemon's startup work, through the chat index's start, has ended). Exact-id attach/info/events read their own session on demand; names and operations requiring the complete index wait for metadata. It binds the socket and --listen address before importing the login shell environment or checking launchers. --ready-fd N writes one line {ready: true, pid, socket, listen, webUrl} to descriptor N and closes it; the log also gets "acpmux ready {...}". _acpmux/status answers at once and reports ready and loginEnv.
daemon.shutdown: The daemon clears any signal mask it inherits, so a launcher that blocks SIGTERM cannot keep it alive. SIGTERM, SIGINT and _acpmux/shutdown remove the socket, detach every agent that runs under an agent host (it keeps running, with its turn and permission prompts, for the next daemon to adopt), stop every other agent (SIGTERM to its process group, SIGKILL to the group after 2 s), save sessions, sync the store and exit, within 5 s. _acpmux/shutdown {endAgents: true} ends hosted agents too, except those of keepSessions, and records each turn in progress as turn_result {status: cancelled, detail: quit}. The CLI follows the same default (cx-qryd0): `acpmux daemon shutdown` keeps hosted agents for the next daemon; `--end-agents` sends endAgents: true; `--keep-agents` is accepted and changes nothing.
